subject: Billing origin and collection flow: who issues invoices and portal opt-in
messages:
From: Lucy Chen <lucy@crimson.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@crimson.com>, AP Team <ap@crimson.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Who will originate invoices / portal integration question

Hi Priya,

Quick question as we're preparing PO 45921: does Redwood originate and send the customer-facing invoice (PDF/e-invoice) or do you prefer invoices to be pulled from our AP portal (Coupa/SAP)? Our AP team prefers to have invoices delivered into the portal to match our internal workflow, but Procurement wants a clear record of the invoice origin for VAT reconciliation.

Also need to confirm the remit-to and whether Redwood can include Crimson Systems' VAT ID on the invoice. If you can send a short note on options (email PDF vs portal push, required headers, and sample invoice header), that would help speed our onboarding.

Thanks,
Lucy Chen
Director, Procurement
Crimson Systems

Attachments: PO_45921.pdf (pdf)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy@crimson.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Who will originate invoices / portal integration question

Hi Lucy — great question. Short answer: we support both approaches. Below are the trade-offs and what we need from you to proceed.

Option A — Redwood issues invoices and emails / sftp push
- Redwood will generate the invoice PDF (with our EIN and your VAT/PO data).
- Delivery methods: email-to-AP, SFTP push, or webhook (invoice XML/PDF).
- Pros: predictable from our side; full audit trail; easy for us to include tax evidence.
- Cons: if your AP system expects the origin to be your vendor network, additional matching steps may be required.

Option B — Use Crimson's AP portal (you pull / receive via Coupa/SAP connector)
- We can enable invoice posting into your portal via EDI/Coupa punchout or SFTP.
- Pros: aligns with your AP workflow and three-way match; likely fewer manual steps for your AP team.
- Cons: we will mark Redwood as the originator in the metadata; for VAT reconciliation we will need explicit header fields from you (VAT ID, remit entity, billing entity).

What we need from Crimson to finalize:
- Preferred delivery method (email PDF to ap@crimson.com, SFTP endpoint, or portal connector).
- Billing contact name + email for invoice copies.
- VAT ID and legal billing name to print on invoices.
- PO number(s) to include on every invoice (you provided PO_45921 — thanks).

I’ve looped in Marissa (Finance) and Connor (Ops) to confirm tax header requirements and any additional compliance checks. We can do the actual connector work after we lock the delivery method.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 415-555-0113

Attachments: Redwood_EIN_and_W9.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Sep 2028 08:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Who will originate invoices / portal integration question

Priya / Connor — quick finance note to include in the reply to Crimson:
- If Redwood is issuing invoices, we will include our EIN and Redwood legal name by default. We need Crimson's VAT ID and legal billing entity to be printed on the invoice to support reverse-charge or local VAT reporting.
- For portal deliveries (Coupa/SAP), please confirm whether the portal requires an XML invoice schema or accepts PDF attachments inside a PO-backed record.
- If Crimson requires consolidated monthly invoicing across multiple Crimson legal entities, we need the entity mapping now (legal name + VAT + remit-to). That will change how we allocate tax lines.

Also, if Crimson wants invoices sent from a Redwood-controlled email address, we can set up branding and DKIM alignment, but that requires a brief DNS TXT entry on their side (we will provide instructions).

Marissa Cole
Senior Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy@crimson.com>, AP Team <ap@crimson.com>, Procurement <procurement@crimson.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Sep 2028 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Who will originate invoices / portal integration question

Hi Lucy — following up with details and a recommendation.

Recommendation: portal-first with email copy
- For Crimson's workflow, we recommend enabling the portal connector (Coupa/SAP) so AP can ingest invoices natively, and we will also send an email copy to ap@crimson.com with the PDF attached for your internal audit folder.
- Required for this flow from Crimson: portal API endpoint or SFTP credentials, billing legal name, VAT ID, remit address, and whether you want Crimson PO displayed as "Customer PO" or "Reference PO" on the invoice header.
- If you need the invoice to show Crimson as the origin for matching, let us know and we can adjust the metadata mapping on our end.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Crimson provides the portal endpoint or confirms SFTP + test credentials.
2) Crimson confirms billing entity details and the PO naming convention.
3) Redwood completes a connector test and sends a sample invoice (no payment due) for Crimson to validate.

I attached our EIN/W-9 for your vendor intake. Once you confirm the preferred delivery method, Marissa will produce the first invoice with PO_45921.

Thanks,
Priya
